title: The Chubby Lock Service（Chubby 锁服务）— IT 论文精读 Paper 20
title_en: The Chubby Lock Service — CS Papers Deep-Read Paper 20

questions.question: Chubby 的作者为什么选择把 Paxos 做成一个锁服务，而不是发给各团队一个共识库？
options: 库方案会让各团队拿到强制锁，而服务只能提供建议锁，从而避免误伤数据
锁服务能把每次读写都经过 Paxos 投票，所以性能比任何库内实现的共识都更高
共识库无法在 5 台机器上运行，只有集中的服务才能凑够过半数所需的副本
单机原型加一把锁、一个小文件就能补上高可用，还顺带能登记谁是主
questions.explanation: 论文的理由很实在：开发者早期不为高可用设计，锁服务让他们事后少量改动就补上；选出主之后还需要一个可靠的地方登记与通告，库不提供；副本成本也被大量客户端摊薄。Chubby 优先的是可用与可靠而非性能，Paxos 只在服务内部跑。
questions.question_en: Why did Chubby's designer package Paxos as a lock service rather than handing teams a consensus library?
options_en: A library would give teams mandatory locks, while a service offers only advisory ones and so avoids corrupting data
A lock service runs every read and write through a Paxos vote, so it outperforms any library implementation of consensus
A consensus library cannot run on five machines; only a central service can gather enough replicas for a majority
A single-machine prototype gains high availability from just a lock and a small file, plus a place to record who the master is
questions.explanation_en: The paper's reasons are practical: developers rarely design for availability up front, and a lock service lets them add it later with minimal changes; after electing a master they also need a reliable place to publish the result, which a library doesn't give; and replica costs are shared across many clients. Chubby prioritizes availability and reliability over performance, and Paxos runs only inside the service.

questions.question: 进程 A 持锁去写存储，中途因 GC 卡住，锁过期后被 B 拿走；随后 A 早先发出的写请求才到达存储。Chubby 的哪个机制专门用来识破它？
options: 客户端缓存失效：主先通知所有缓存作废，A 的写请求因此被自动丢弃
序列号：令牌里带每次换主就加一的世代号，存储服务据此拒绝过期令牌
主租约：租约期内其余副本不另选新主，所以 A 的锁不会被 B 拿到
KeepAlive 宽限期：A 在宽限期内重连，会话延续后它的写请求就合法了
questions.explanation: 迟到的旧消息要靠序列号治：持锁者把令牌随请求发给存储，存储校验后拒绝旧令牌；不便改造的存储则用 lock-delay 退而求其次。缓存失效保证的是读不脏，主租约防的是 Chubby 自己的脑裂，都管不到外部存储收到的迟到写。
questions.question_en: Process A holds a lock and writes to storage, stalls in GC, its lock expires and B takes it; then A's earlier write finally arrives. Which Chubby mechanism exists to catch this?
options_en: Cache invalidation: the master first tells every cache to drop the entry, so A's write is discarded automatically
Sequencers: the token carries a generation number bumped on each new master, so storage rejects stale tokens
The master lease: other replicas won't elect a new master during the lease, so B can never take A's lock
The KeepAlive grace period: A reconnects within it, the session continues, and its write becomes valid again
questions.explanation_en: Late messages are handled by sequencers: the holder sends the token with its request and storage rejects outdated ones; lock-delay is the weaker fallback for storage that can't be modified. Cache invalidation keeps reads fresh and the master lease prevents split-brain inside Chubby; neither touches a late write reaching an outside store.

questions.question: Chubby 只用 5 台副本就能服务数以万计的客户端，最主要靠的是什么？
options: 锁粗粒度、一持有就是几小时，加上缓存与主动失效把读挡在本地
每个客户端都参与 Paxos 投票，共识的计算负担被摊到了数万台机器上
写操作不必等过半数副本落盘，主收到后立即返回，因此吞吐很高
客户端缓存采用定时过期，偶尔读到旧数据换来了主几乎零的读负载
questions.explanation: 整个设计赌的是读远多于写、锁很稀疏：粗粒度锁让抢锁稀少，缓存加主动失效让读既不脏又不打到主，RPC 流量大多是 KeepAlive。客户端从不碰共识，写也必须过半数落盘；定时过期是 DNS 的做法，Chubby 的缓存是严格一致的。
questions.question_en: What mainly lets a five-replica Chubby cell serve tens of thousands of clients?
options_en: Coarse-grained locks held for hours, plus client caches with active invalidation that keep almost all reads local
Every client takes part in the Paxos vote, so the work of consensus is spread across tens of thousands of machines
Writes don't wait for a majority of replicas to persist; the master acknowledges at once, so throughput is high
Client caches expire on a timer, accepting occasional stale reads in exchange for near-zero read load on the master
questions.explanation_en: The design bets that reads vastly outnumber writes and locks are rare: coarse locks keep acquisitions sparse, and caching with active invalidation keeps reads fresh without hitting the master, so most RPCs are KeepAlives. Clients never touch consensus, writes still need a majority on disk, and timed expiry is DNS's approach; Chubby's cache is strictly consistent.
